slides.title: Timo, the In-Car AI Social Robot, Launches on Kickstarter
slides.highlight: Timo is an in-car AI social robot, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Former Li Auto AI Chief Scientist Chen Wei Raises Funds for Embodied AI Home Robot Startup
slides.tldr: FUNDING FOR EMBODIED AI HOME ROBOTS
slides.highlight: Chen Wei has raised funds for an embodied AI startup focused on home robots, which aligns with RwB's interest in embodied social robots.

slides.title: ABM-SIRTEM: A Hybrid Agent-Based and Epidemiological Model for Pandemic Response
slides.highlight: This hybrid model integrates individual-level economic productivity and welfare with disease dynamics, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis.

card.one_liner: A hybrid model coupling population-level disease dynamics with agent-based simulations of socioeconomic compliance behavior.
card.key_idea: Integrates SIRTEM epidemiological modeling with an ABM using evolutionary game theory to update agent compliance based on economic productivity, mental well-being, and health risks.
card.evaluation: Calibrated using historical COVID-19 test counts and restriction indices from four U.S. states; positive-test trajectories broadly reproduced observed waves.
card.limitation: Assessments reflect calibration fit rather than performance on held-out data; some states showed substantial underestimation of negative-test counts.

slides.title: ECHO: A Matched-Contrast Benchmark for Context-Sensitive Turn-Taking in Full-Duplex Dialogue
slides.highlight: This work introduces a benchmark for distinguishing between interruptions and backchannels in full-duplex dialogue, supporting HyECHO's goals in addressee/listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: ECHO is a diagnostic benchmark for Chinese full-duplex dialogue to evaluate context-sensitive turn-taking decisions.
card.key_idea: Uses matched-contrast pairs with identical insertion text but different dialogue contexts to distinguish between interruptions (Yield) and backchannels/off-talk (Keep), employing a Pairwise Action Success Rate metric.
card.evaluation: Evaluated four speech systems and Gemini (text reference) using PASR and PKC; results show most speech systems exhibit a strong Yield bias.
card.limitation: Relies on synthesized audio, reducing ecological validity, and does not fully isolate dialogue context from acoustic factors like speaker-reference variation.

slides.title: Audio-Visual Turn-taking Prediction in Cocktail Party Scenarios
slides.highlight: This research evaluates audio-visual predictive turn-taking models in noisy cocktail-party scenarios, providing insights into modality-specific degradation and adaptation. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling in complex environments.

card.one_liner: Predictive turn-taking models struggle in cocktail-party scenarios, but multimodal fine-tuning improves robustness against noise.
card.key_idea: Evaluates Voice Activity Projection (VAP) variants (Audio, Video, and Multimodal) by pre-training on clean Candor data and fine-tuning on the noisy AVCocktail dataset.
card.evaluation: Tested on Candor and AVCocktail datasets using weighted F1 scores. Results show MM-VAP is most robust, with up to 30% relative improvement after fine-tuning.
card.limitation: Fine-tuning causes catastrophic forgetting of the original domain; current fusion mechanisms fail to fully exploit audio-visual complementarity in high noise.

slides.title: Rethinking the Implications of Human Feedback for Preference Learning in Human-Robot Collaboration
slides.tldr: IMPROVING ROBOT PREFERENCE LEARNING VIA DYNAMIC IMPLICATION MODELING
slides.highlight: The proposed IMPLIED method improves how robots infer human preferences from feedback during collaboration, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: IMPLIED improves robot preference learning by dynamically revising implication labels for unchosen actions using feedback.
card.key_idea: A mixture model combining a fixed-rule prior with a Gaussian Process classifier that learns to infer and revise accepted/rejected labels for unchosen actions based on direct evidence.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via simulation (sandwich-making, block-sorting) and a physical pizza-making study against fixed-rule and LLM baselines using L2 error, F1 score, and conflict proportion.

slides.title: Exploring Multimodal Turn-Taking Cues in Face-to-Face Conversation using Voice Activity Projection
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that incorporating visual features like facial action units, gaze, and pose improves turn-taking prediction over audio-only models, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception.

card.one_liner: Visual features from face-to-face conversations significantly improve turn-taking prediction over audio-only models.
card.key_idea: Extends Voice Activity Projection (VAP) by fusing audio with visual features (FAU, gaze, body, head) using cross-attention, delta motion features, and trainable gating mechanisms.
card.evaluation: Tested on 400 hours of Meta Seamless Interaction dataset using VAP loss and balanced accuracy for hold/shift, short/long, and pre-shift tasks.
card.limitation: Results may be upper-bounded as test splits are not dyad-disjoint, and gaze estimates are unreliable during eye occlusion.

slides.title: Gaze as Evidence for Common Grounding: A Cross-Corpus Analysis of MapTask and MUNDEX
slides.tldr: GAZE AS A CUE FOR COMMON GROUNDING
slides.highlight: This research examines how gaze features correlate with grounding and reference interpretation in collaborative tasks, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: Gaze patterns consistently signal grounding across different collaborative tasks, most notably for the task leader.
card.key_idea: Mapping MapTask and MUNDEX gaze ontologies to a shared partner/task/away vocabulary to analyze associations between gaze features and grounding states.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via Mann-Whitney U tests, GEE, and logistic regression (macro-F1) on MapTask and MUNDEX; results show modest predictive gains over controls.
card.limitation: Small effect sizes, limited number of participants, and sensitivity of results to the unit of inference (dialogue vs. participant).

slides.title: PRISM: Predictive Representation of Interaction Style and Motion for Social Robot Navigation
slides.highlight: PRISM uses a transformer encoder to infer human interaction traits from passive observations, improving collision rates and navigation efficiency in crowds. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and social robots.

card.one_liner: PRISM infers pedestrian interaction styles from passive observation to improve social robot navigation safety.
card.key_idea: A transformer encoder uses Rank-N-Contrast loss to map trajectories into a continuous ordinal latent space, providing style vectors and temporal confidence scores to a navigation policy.
card.evaluation: Evaluated in PyBullet simulations using ORCA pedestrians; PRISM reduced collision rates (e.g., 0.19 to 0.12) compared to the HEIGHT geometry-only baseline.
card.limitation: Results are limited to synthetic ORCA-based heterogeneity; lacks real-world pedestrian data and statistical significance claims via confidence intervals.

slides.title: Negation Beyond the Verbal Channel: Temporal Multimodal Correlates in Dialogue
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that nonverbal behaviors, particularly facial features, can predict negation cues in dialogue, supporting HyECHO's goal of non-data-hungry multimodal social perception.

card.one_liner: Nonverbal behavior can reliably distinguish spoken negation cues from control words without lexical or acoustic input.
card.key_idea: Using 20 time-series models as probes, the study analyzes multimodal event streams (gaze, face, body, hands) around negation cues in VR-based human-human interviews.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 27 VR interviews using 10-fold cross-validation; RocketPFN achieved the highest mean AUROC (.728). Results are robust across multiple time-series classifiers.
card.limitation: Findings are limited to a single VR setting, a German-language corpus dominated by the word 'nicht', and explicitly marked negation cues.

slides.title: Online Multimodal Workload Assessment in Contact-Rich Physical Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This paper introduces a transparent framework for assessing interaction workload in contact-rich pHRI using interaction wrench, kinematics, and skin conductance. It is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: An interpretable multimodal framework for online interaction workload assessment in contact-rich physical human-robot interaction.
card.key_idea: Integrates interaction wrench, TCP kinematics, and skin conductance into four interpretable factors, using path curvature and task progression for context-adaptive weighting.
card.evaluation: Evaluated with 24 participants across 18 environmental conditions; used leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) validation against pupil diameter and learning-based baselines (MLP, TCN, LSTM).
card.limitation: Correspondence with the physiological reference is weak near task onset (ρ_early = 0.002).

slides.title: EMoG: Emotion-Modulated Gait Generation for Expressive Humanoid Locomotion
slides.highlight: This framework enables expressive humanoid locomotion by using an emotion-modulated gait generation system, supporting the RwB goal of enhancing human-robot interaction through embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: EMoG enables humanoid robots to perform expressive, emotion-modulated walking via controllable gait generation and tracking.
card.key_idea: A lightweight MLP generates periodic gait trajectories conditioned on an emotional-style code and physical commands, which are then executed by a unified RL motion tracker.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via user recognition studies, MuJoCo simulations, and Unitree G1 hardware tests. EMoG showed higher completion rates and better command tracking than baselines.
card.limitation: Emotion recognition is category-dependent and decreases after physical execution; style intensity is not yet perceptually calibrated.

slides.title: DiaWhisper-DPO: Role-Attributed Transcription of Clinical Interviews via Failure-Mined Preference Optimization
slides.highlight: This work introduces DiaWhisper-DPO, an end-to-end model for transcription and role attribution that reduces error propagation compared to cascaded systems. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on diarization and identity recognition within human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: DiaWhisper-DPO enables end-to-end role-attributed transcription of clinical interviews using failure-mined preference optimization.
card.key_idea: LoRA-tuned Whisper-large-v3 with an auxiliary role head, refined via DPO using genuine decoding failures as rejected completions to eliminate repetition loops and improve stability.
card.evaluation: Tested on DAIC-WOZ and PDCH-HAMD against cascaded baselines; achieved 0.973 role accuracy and 0.119 DER on DAIC-WOZ, significantly reducing seed variation.
card.limitation: DAIC-WOZ evaluation relies on synthetic interviewer audio; outputs still require human verification for clinical use.

slides.title: Neuro-Symbolic Hierarchical Intention Anticipation in Human Behavior
slides.highlight: This research presents a neuro-symbolic framework for anticipating human goals across four ontological levels, supporting MIMIC's focus on neuro-symbolic agent models for simulating human-AI interaction.

card.one_liner: A neuro-symbolic framework for anticipating human goals by combining neural prediction with hierarchical symbolic constraints.
card.key_idea: A Hierarchical Planning Decoder (HPD) attached to a frozen encoder, using soft neuro-symbolic regularization and hard reachability masks to ensure ontological validity across four levels.
card.evaluation: Tested on 15,002 multimodal episodes (NTU RGB+D 120). Outperformed sequential baselines in top-5 accuracy and joint logic constraint satisfaction.
card.limitation: Challenges remain regarding compositional goal generalization and the prediction of unordered sets.
